sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt: A data set records 12, 19, 12, 13, 15. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 13, median 14.2
mean 14.2, median 14
mean 14.2, median 13
mean 14, median 13

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 202 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 8 yes, 27 no; row 2: 10 yes, 16 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 7x + 8, where x is measured in kilometre travelleds and y in litres of fuel. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional litres of fuel is associated with 7 more kilometre travelleds.
Each additional kilometre travelled causes an increase of exactly 7 litres of fuel.
Each additional kilometre travelled is associated with an increase of about 7 litres of fuel.
The predicted value is 7 litres of fuel when x is 0.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.

choices: Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
